title: Git Bisect for Your Data
why_read: A clever and concrete application of database branching to binary-search through time for finding when a data bug was introduced is a genuinely useful technique worth reading in detail.
analysis: The article proposes applying the git-bisect concept to data debugging: instead of scrolling through logs, use database branching (via Neon's copy-on-write branches) to instantly recreate the database state at any past timestamp and query it directly. It reports concrete numbers, such as roughly 1.7 seconds per branch-and-query probe, letting a 24-hour window at one-minute precision be searched in about 13 probes instead of 1,440 full scans. This is a practical and clever technique that generalizes an already-loved workflow (git bisect) to a common and painful class of problem, tracking down when data corruption started. It's a solid, concrete engineering idea with real numbers backing it up, making it more valuable than a typical listicle-style post.
